title: Bug/4912 GitGraph routing and colouring for merges and cherry-picks
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

Fixes issues with colouring and routing of merges in GitGraph.

Resolves #4912 

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

- Changed commit variable names `commit1` and `commit2` to `commitA` and `commitB` respectively, to prevent confusion with `seq` property values (which are also numbers and used to ID the commits).
- Refactored `hasOverlappingCommits` function to be easier to read and renamed it `shouldRerouteArrow`:
  - Used `Array.some()` instead of `Array.filter()` (should increase performance with larger graphs, if needed)
  - Swapped out `Object.keys()` for `Object.values()`
  - It takes a new argument: the name of the branch which would receive the arrow's curve and thereby causing issues for overlapping commits.
- Introduced branch colour assignments to each conditional check for routing.
- New e2e tests (many based on reviews by @nirname and @mathbraga)
- Added more sample diagrams to demo folder show how the graphs should look in different situations.

### :clipboard: Tasks

Make sure you

- [x] :book: have read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] :computer: have added necessary unit/e2e tests.
- [x] :notebook: have added documentation. Make sure [`MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION`](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/develop/packages/mermaid/src/docs/community/development.md#3-update-documentation) is used for all new features.

comments.author: mathbraga
comments.body:
Hi, I believe `commitX.branch` returns `undefined`. `Object.entries()` returns arrays containing the pair `[key, value]`, so calling `commitX.branch` is like doing `[key, value].branch` which should return `undefined`.

One solution could be:

```
allCommits[commitX[0]].branch
```
comments.label_reasoning: The reviewer identifies that commitX.branch returns undefined because Object.entries() returns [key, value] arrays, not objects — this is incorrect usage of the API/data structure returned by Object.entries().

comments.author: guypursey
comments.body:
I think you're right re `Object.entries()`. It should have been `Object.values()`.

Your fix would also work but I don't think we need the key for anything, so grabbing just the values saves us having to make a second look-up (and with any luck, makes the function clearer).

Good catch 👍

comments.author: nirname
comments.body: Should not this code be a part of `shouldRerouteArrow` function? It is not used anywhere else. Would not comparison of `seq` do effectively the same as comparison of x / y?
comments.label_reasoning: The reviewer suggests moving code into the shouldRerouteArrow function since it is only used there, pointing to a structural/organization issue with how the code is divided across functions.

comments.author: guypursey
comments.body:
Hi, thanks for taking a look.

 - Re the `shouldRerouteArrow` function: I originally wanted to keep the number of new arguments passed to `shouldRerouteArrow` to a minimum. But you're right: I could pass it `p1` and `p2` and do the calculation for `branchToGetCurve` inside `shouldRerouteArrow`. I can try that out.

 - Re `seq`: I don't think comparing `seq` would do what's needed -- it would only tell you whether one commit comes *before or after* the other in sequence. But here we need to know whether one commit is *above or below* the other (or, in case of `dir === TB`, to the *left or right*). This then tells us if the normal branch curve will be okay or will cause a conflict that requires rerouting.

comments.author: guypursey
comments.body:
This is how I've understood it:

- When `dir === 'TB'`, `seq` will give you the order of commits going from top to bottom on the `y` axis. But we need to know where they are on the `x` axis, going to left to right, to know how the curve might be drawn and whether we need to reroute.

- When `dir === 'LR'`, `seq` will give you the order of commits going from left to right on the `x` axis. But we need to know where the commits are on the `y` axis, going to top to bottom, to know how the curve might be drawn and whether we need to reroute.

Hope that makes sense.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests refactoring by moving code into the shouldRerouteArrow function and questions whether comparing seq would be equivalent, implying a code restructuring change.

comments.author: nirname
comments.body: It would be more portable if a function would not have side effects and closures like `dir`, but since it is only for this files and other anonymous functions do the same, that is ok.
comments.label_reasoning: The reviewer flags that the function relies on side effects and closures (e.g., dir), which affects portability and encapsulation — a design-level concern about function purity and dependency on outer scope.

comments.author: guypursey
comments.body:
Yes, I agree. This is was my reasoning for putting `branchToGetCurve` check outside this function originally -- to try to keep this function pure.

Because it calls on `dir`, I thought it would be better alongside the other `dir` checks in `drawArrow` which is already impure. But I moved it inside based on your last review comment.

There are lots of messy/impure functions in this page, I think -- I would like to rewrite in a separate PR sometime.

comments.author: nirname
comments.body:
I feel like this function signature can be simplified down to
```
shouldRerouteArrow(commitA, commitB, allCommits);
```
I know that it may seem redundant to get p1 and p2 inside the function once again but the access time of commitPos is O(1) and there is no cases when we have to pass positions independently from commits.

What do you think?
comments.label_reasoning: The reviewer proposes simplifying the function signature by removing redundant position parameters (p1, p2) since they can always be derived from the commit objects, which is a function signature/consistency concern.

comments.author: guypursey
comments.body:
Yes, this is another reason I had originally put `branchToGetCurve` outside the `shouldRerouteArrow` function -- to keep the signature for `shouldRerouteArrow` as simple as possible.

I also thought about recalculating `p1` and `p2` inside `shouldRerouteArrow` as you suggest. But I felt it was redundant/repetitive (violating DRY principle) so decided to pass them as arguments. I was thinking less about performance (which is minimal as you say) and more about confusion/readability.

I think a lot more refactoring could be done overall but I don't want to get too much scope creep for this issue/PR.

Some of things I will rewrite in a fix for #4932 (which I have already started working on locally).

comments.author: nirname
comments.body:
`shouldRerouteArrow` function violates DRY anyway, because it uses `dir` property. In case we consider this function as a method or instance-related function it can use all object attributes without referencing the object directly (this, self ...etc). In case we consider this function as a pure one, we have to pass everything as arguments including `dir`. Right now this is neither of these two. That is why I have suggested to stick to previous signature.

Btw, I am ok with how it looks now. Simply looking for better options.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests simplifying the function signature to shouldRerouteArrow(commitA, commitB, allCommits) by removing p1 and p2 parameters, which is a concrete refactoring suggestion.
